title: Sunset Session

conditions.headline: Nvidia undertow drags tech, but the week still rides in
conditions.summary: Tech sank as Nvidia hit new lows after its CEO resigned, pulling the Nasdaq down 0.9% while the Dow edged higher. Stocks still logged their first winning week since early October.

sections.title: Closing Bell
items: S&P 500 fell 0.4% to 7,561.67; Nasdaq dropped 0.9% to 25,136.27; Dow rose 0.1% to 52,347.55; Russell 2000 slipped 0.3% to 2,790.49.
Stocks opened higher, then slid as tech sold off, with the S&P down about 0.9% at midday before recovering part of the loss.
Nvidia fell to new 52-week lows a day after CEO Jensen Huang resigned; CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO.
Technology lost about 2% while the other sectors closed higher, led by consumer staples, communication services and energy.
It was the first winning week since early October: S&P +2.5%, Nasdaq +2.3%, Dow +2.1%.

sections.title: Macro & Fed
items: October PPI rose 0.3% vs. 0.4% expected; core PPI rose 0.3%, in line.
Producer prices are up 6.5% from a year earlier, the biggest annual rise since November 2022.
Boston Fed's Susan Collins said more policy tightening is warranted soon; Chicago Fed's Austan Goolsbee said the Fed has work to do on credibility.
Futures point to a quarter-point rate hike at the December 8-9 Fed meeting.
The 10-year Treasury yield rose about 5 basis points to roughly 5.15%, up nearly 30 basis points on the week; the dollar index hit its highest level since April 2025.

sections.title: Biggest Movers
items: MOD (Modine): about +28% — report that Samsung is exploring a deal to buy the company.
NU (Nu Holdings): about +11% — fintech names in favor.
CBRS (Cerebras): about +10% — surprise profit and raised 2026 revenue outlook.
META (Meta Platforms): about +3% — gained with communication services strength.
AMD (Advanced Micro Devices): about -9% — chip stocks sold off alongside Nvidia.
CSCO (Cisco): about -6% — beat and raised, but slower non-hyperscaler orders and margin worries weighed.
NVDA (Nvidia): lower, at 52-week lows — fallout from the CEO's resignation and analyst target cuts.
NBIS (Nebius): about -12% — guided 2026 revenue to the low end of its range.

sections.title: Earnings Today & Tonight
items: Cisco's late-Thursday report beat on revenue and earnings and raised full-year guidance, but shares fell today.
Applied Materials beat estimates and guided above consensus, yet the stock dipped after a downgrade.
Cerebras rallied after posting a surprise profit and lifting its 2026 outlook.
No major companies reported after today's close.

sections.title: Business News
items: Anthropic's IPO is set to price Wednesday at $70 to $78 a share and begin trading Thursday.
A global Microsoft 365 outage disrupted Teams and Outlook; Microsoft said it was not caused by malicious activity.
Senate Banking leaders asked Jensen Huang and Commerce Secretary Lutnick to testify about Nvidia chip sales in Asia.
Arm slipped after a report its CEO was approached in Nvidia's CEO search.
WTI crude settled near $88.56, little changed; bitcoin fell below $70,000 for the first time since late August.

sections.title: On Deck
items: Monday 7:30 AM CT: Empire State manufacturing index.
Monday 8:05 AM CT: New York Fed President John Williams speaks; 11:00 AM CT: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh speaks.
Before the open: Baidu, Tyson Foods, XPeng, Aramark.
After the close: AECOM, Powell Industries.
Looking ahead: Nvidia reports Tuesday afternoon; retail sales also Tuesday.

script: Cowabunga! This is Surf Daddy, your local Kahuna, live from Surfside USA to all you Trade Wind surfers from the Gulf Coast to the North Shore. It's Friday, November thirteenth, twenty twenty-six, and this is your Sunset Session, the full wrap of today's market. The sun is sliding into the water, the last set of the week is rolling in, and I'm waxing the board for next week. Gus the wonder dog sat on the deck all afternoon, guarding the cooler and counting waves. Give the crew a good evening woof, Gus! Here's the final set. It was a mixed and choppy close. The S and P five hundred slipped four tenths of a percent to seven thousand five hundred sixty-two. The Nasdaq dropped nine tenths of a percent to twenty-five thousand one hundred thirty-six. The Dow eked out a gain of one tenth of a percent to fifty-two thousand three hundred forty-eight. The Russell two thousand eased three tenths of a percent. Stocks opened higher, then wiped out by midday before paddling back in the afternoon. Tech was the weak spot, down about two percent, while every other sector finished in the green, led by consumer staples, communication services and energy. Even so, it was the first winning week since early October, with the S and P up about two and a half percent for the week. The gnarly current today was Nvidia. Shares hit new fifty-two week lows a day after chief executive Jensen Huang resigned following reports about his personal conduct. Now the wind and weather. Producer prices rose three tenths of a percent in October, a touch cooler than expected. But they are up six and a half percent from a year ago, the hottest pace since late twenty twenty-two. Boston Fed President Susan Collins said more tightening is warranted soon, and traders are betting on a rate hike at the December meeting. The ten year Treasury yield climbed about five basis points to roughly five point one five percent, and the dollar firmed. Oil was little changed near eighty-eight and a half dollars, gold was flat, and bitcoin slipped below seventy thousand dollars. Over in the lineup, A M D wiped out, down around nine percent. Cisco fell around six percent even after a strong quarter, as investors fretted over slower orders and margins. The big wave belonged to Modine. Shares surged about twenty-eight percent on a report that Samsung is exploring a deal to buy the company. Modine rode that one all the way to the beach. Gus, that's worth a biscuit! Here you go, buddy! Cerebras, still a grommet from its May listing, jumped about ten percent after raising its outlook. On the tide chart, Applied Materials beat estimates and guided higher, but the stock still dipped. Tonight was quiet, with no big names reporting after the bell. Beach talk: Anthropic's huge stock offering is set to price next Wednesday, and a Microsoft outage knocked out Teams and Outlook in dozens of countries. Tomorrow's forecast covers Monday. The Empire State manufacturing survey lands at seven thirty A M Central. New York Fed President John Williams speaks at eight oh five, and Fed Chair Kevin Warsh at eleven A M Central. Baidu and Tyson Foods report before the open, and AECOM reports after the close. Nvidia's earnings arrive Tuesday afternoon. Catch the Dawn Patrol Monday morning for the first swell of the week.
